script_text: Bienvenidos a esta clase sobre Impl 36 SystemSetup Print layouts en SAP Business One. En esta lección exploraremos las mejores prácticas de consultoría, flujos operativos y configuraciones del sistema. System Setup & Administration: Print Layouts SAP Business One Version 10.0 This topic covers print layouts which are required for the printing of documents and reports.

Objectives Objectives: Describe the function of a print layout Set default print layouts for users and by business partner Use the Report and Layout Manager for managing reports and print layouts Define a printing sequence for a document On completion of this topic, you will be able to: Describe the function of a print layout Set default print layouts for users and by business partner Use the Report and Layout Manager for managing reports and print layouts Define a printing sequence for a document

Print Layout Concept SAP Business One Each marketing document or report has a print layout This is a template for how the on screen document will look in printed form Printed documents Layout Layout Print layouts are templates that define how an on screen document or report will look when it is printed. SAP provides a set of predefined layouts for each marketing document. You can use these right out of the box or you can edit them to create client specific printed documents. This is typically done for external facing documents, but you can also customize the layouts for internally used documents such as pick lists and bills of materials. You can also create new print layouts for customized reports that you develop.

Print Layouts for a Document A document can have multiple print layouts To preview a document in the available layouts, open a document and choose File > Preview Layouts… The default layout is marked in bold There can be multiple print layouts for a document. To see the available print layouts, open a document and choose the preview layouts option from the File menu. The layouts available for the current document type are shown. Then select a layout to view the printed document. The one in bold is the default template that will be used when this user prints this document. You should decide with the customer which templates will be required for each document. For example, an A R invoice can be printed as a packing list as well as an invoice. Note: If you print or preview a document before you add it to the system, the system automatically adds the Draft watermark to the printout.

Setting the Default Print Layout A default layout can be specified for all users, for the current user only, or for specified users You can also set a default for all business partners or for specified business partners Authorization required to set default layout It is quite possible that users might need to use more than one print layout template for a document. A user might need to use an invoice layout for each of their customers’ languages, or set a different invoice layout for certain groups of customers. Authorized users can set a different layout to be used as default for different users or business partners. To set the default layout, open a document and choose the Layout Designer icon from the icon toolbar. This opens a window where you can choose another layout and set as default. A new template can be set as default for: All users The current user only Specific users that you select from the list of users You can also set the layout as default for: All business partners for which a default template has not yet been assigned Selected business partners – this allows you to select one or more business partners. Note: To be authorized to change the default print layout for a document or report, the general authorization General Change Default Report is required.

Customizing Print Layouts Print layouts need to be customized to meet the customer’s needs for external facing documents You can also translate print layouts to provide documents in the customer’s native language To save time during an implementation, demonstrate the various print layouts available for a document, and identify a layout as the base for changes Print layouts need to be customized during an implementation project to meet the customer’s needs for external facing documents. You will need at minimum to insert the company’s logo and address. You might need to translate the print layout to provide printed documents in a customer’s native language. These changes can take a considerable amount of time. During an implementation you should demonstrate the various print layouts to the customer. When you identify a layout that best fits the customer’s needs, you can use that layout as the base for changes.

Managing Print Layouts and Reports Administration Setup General Report and Layout Manager Report and Layout Manager is the central point for managing print layouts and user reports When you select a document type you will see all the print layouts for that document type The Report and Layout Manager is the central point for managing print layouts and also user reports. When you install SAP Business One, print layouts for documents and reports are loaded according to the localization. You can view and manage these print layouts using the Report and Layout Manager. You can browse the list, or search for a named report or layout. When you select a document type you will see all the print layouts for that document type. There are different layouts for item type and service type documents.
Managing Print Layouts and Reports (cont.) You can also access the Report and Layout Manager by choosing the Layout Designer icon from an open document. Then choose the Manage Layout button.

Editing Print Layouts All new layouts are provided in Crystal Reports Older layouts are provided in Print Layout Designer (PLD) To change a print layout, select the layout and choose Edit After you make your changes you will save the layout with a new name Print layouts are provided in either Crystal Reports (CR) or Print Layout Designer (PLD) format. All new print layouts from SAP Business One are written in Crystal Reports. To change a print layout, select the layout and choose Edit. After you have made your changes you will save the layout with a new name. It is not possible to directly modify a print layout provided in SAP Business One. Note: You cannot delete the reports and layouts that are provided with the core product.

Editing Print Layout Designer Layouts When you edit a PLD layout, the system opens the Print Layout Designer tool After you choose Edit, and if the print layout is the Print Layout Designer type, the built in Print Layout Designer tool will automatically open, allowing you to edit and save the layout. The detailed steps for editing a print layout are not covered in this topic. For more information on editing a print layout, see the how to guide How to Customize Printing Layouts with the Print Layout Designer.

Editing Crystal Reports Layouts When you edit a Crystal Reports layout, the system opens SAP Crystal Reports for SAP Business One If the print layout is the Crystal Reports type, the system automatically opens SAP Crystal Reports for SAP Business One designer. This allows you to edit the layout and save it as a new layout. Crystal Reports Designer is required and must be installed in order to edit layouts. The detailed steps for editing a print layout are not covered in this topic. For more information on editing a print layout, see the how to guide How to Work with Crystal Reports in SAP Business One.

Crystal Integration SAP Crystal Reports integration for SAP Business One is provided with the installation files After you make changes to a print layout, you can save it directly in SAP Business One using the Add ins menu You can also preview how the changes will look in SAP Business One SAP Crystal Reports integration for the SAP Business One application is provided with the installation files for SAP Business One. Once the integration package is installed, SAP Business One is shown as a data source in Crystal Reports and the SAP Business One tables match the application menu structure. There are additional functions that are specific for SAP Business One, such as drill downs and selection criteria. After you make changes to a print layout, you can save it directly in SAP Business One using the Add ins menu. The new layout will then show in the list of layouts in the Report and Layout Manager window. You can also preview how the changes will look in SAP Business One.

Import and Export (Modified Crystal Reports Layouts) Export and Import wizards allow you to move modified Crystal Reports print layouts between SAP Business One companies Layouts are packaged as b1px file Wizards also support import and export of user defined reports developed in Crystal Reports You can export Crystal Reports layouts that you have modified to another SAP Business One system. This can save time during the course of a SAP Business One implementation, when you need to move templates from one company to another, or to apply a layout to different types of documents. To export print layouts, choose Export. A wizard opens, allowing you to select the layouts for export. The selected layouts are exported as a package ( .b1px file type) and can only be imported into another SAP Business One system. To import layouts, choose Import. You can also use these buttons to import and export user defined reports developed in Crystal Reports.

Master Layouts You can import a Crystal Reports layout as a master layout for other document types When you import a Crystal Reports layout you can specify a layout as a master layout for other document types. This enables you to make common changes, such as company logo, in one layout and use this layout for other documents with a similar structure. For example, a master layout that is created for a sales invoice can be applied to sales quotations or deliveries. Master layouts can be applied to sales, purchasing, inventory and production document types. When you import the package file: In the Report and Layout Selection window, select the Master Layout checkbox In the Set Master Layout window, select the other document types to which you want to assign this layout. Fine tune the duplicated layouts as needed. For example, you should update text fields that refer to the document type, and delete or add fields based on the specific document type. Note: You can also duplicate a PLD layout to create a new PLD layout for another document type. The utility is located under the menu Administration > Utilities > Duplicate Layout Template.

Printing Sequence Use the Printing Seqs tab to define the set of print layouts to be printed for a print layout You can include other document types in the printing sequence You can set a sequence as default for when you print a document The sequence of layouts to be printed for the A R invoice layout Different companies have different printing needs and procedures. Perhaps a company wants to always include a packing slip or a delivery note when they print an invoice for a customer. This can easily be done using a printing sequence. In the Report and Layout Manager window, select a print layout, then choose the printing sequence tab and create a new sequence. The sample printing sequence shown here will first print a packing list, followed by two copies of a delivery note, followed by the A R invoice using the default print layout followed by a tax only invoice. You simply select from the available print layouts. You can also select the printer for each document. After you create a printing sequence for a document type, it appears in the Layout Designer window and you can set it as a default for the document.

Summary Key points from this topic: A print layout defines how an on screen document looks when printed SAP provides predefined print layouts for each marketing document. A document may have several available print layouts, and you can assign different default layouts to different users. During the implementation, you edit the print layouts to meet the customer’s need for external facing documents. The Report and Layout Manager is the central point for managing print layouts and reports. You can edit Crystal Reports layouts using the Crystal Reports Designer. Older print layouts can be edited using the Print Layout Designer tool which is part of SAP Business One. Using the Report and Layout Manager, you can export modified Crystal layouts and user defined reports to another SAP Business One system. When you import Crystal Reports print layouts, you can designate a master layout to apply to multiple document types. You can duplicate a PLD print layout as a template for another document. You can define a printing sequence for a document to include number of copies, printer, and any additional document types Here are some key points to take from this topic: A print layout defines how an on screen document looks when printed SAP provides predefined print layouts for each marketing document. A document may have several available print layouts, and you can assign different default layouts to different users. During the implementation, you need to edit the print layouts to meet the customer’s need for external facing documents. The Report and Layout Manager is the central point for managing print layouts, and also for managing reports. You can edit Crystal Reports layouts using the Crystal Reports Designer. Older print layouts can be edited using the Print Layout Designer tool which is part of SAP Business One. An integration package is provided to integrate Crystal layouts with SAP Crystal Reports. Using the Report and Layout Manager, you can export modified Crystal layouts and user defined reports, and import them on another SAP Business One system. When you import Crystal Reports print layouts as a package, you can designate a master layout and apply it to multiple document types. You can duplicate a layout of type print layout designer (PLD) as a template for another document. You can define a printing sequence for a document to include number of copies, printer, and any additional document types.
